newsitem.title: UK: UK's CBI attacks Labour windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: UK's CBI attacks Labour windfall tax.

text.p: The Confederation of British Insustry on Thursday criticised opposition Labour party proposals for a windfall tax on privatised utilities as an "arbitrary tax" that could hurt inward investment to Britain.

CBI chief economist Kate Barker told a conference on the impact of a Labour government on business that the levy would set "a very disturbing precedent for people who are thinking of investing in the UK."
She said the business community had serious objections to the tax irrespective of the level and irrespective of the particular utilities that would be affected.

Barker also criticised the retrospective nature of the proposed tax, saying it would hit present shareholders, who may not have benefited from high profits and dividends from the companies in the past.
Labour has said it would use proceeds from a windfall tax to fund a programme for the unemployed. The party has not yet specified which privatised companies would be subject to the levy.
